result.name: Picard classes and the Néron–Severi quotient
result.statement: On P¹×P¹, NS(X)=Pic(X)≅Z² with fiber-class intersection matrix [[0,1],[1,0]]. The class (a,b) has self-intersection 2ab. For a,b≥0, its space of sections has dimension (a+1)(b+1).
result.proof: The projective-bundle description of the product gives the two independent fiber classes and no Pic⁰ component. Two fibers of the same projection are disjoint and equivalent, so each fiber class squares to zero. A fiber of one projection meets a fiber of the other in one point; bilinearity gives (aF₁+bF₂)²=2ab. Sections of O(a,b) are bihomogeneous polynomials of bidegree (a,b). Their monomial basis consists of the (a+1) choices of first-factor exponent and (b+1) choices of second-factor exponent, proving the dimension formula directly. These explicit calculations use the product structure; they do not imply that Picard groups of arbitrary varieties are free of rank two.

example.calculation: The first class has twelve independent sections and self-intersection twelve. The second has two sections and self-intersection zero. Both are discrete divisor classes, whereas on an elliptic curve the degree-zero line bundles form a positive-dimensional Picard variety and cannot be replaced by a single rank count.
example.conclusion: The finite-rank divisor quotient is a well-defined geometric object. It is different from an unspecified real vector space obtained by tensoring every line bundle with R.

result.proof: Differentiate S[x+εξ,y+εη] at ε=0 and integrate the velocity terms by parts. Endpoint terms vanish, leaving δS=∫(E_xξ+E_yη)dt.
